_comment: System packages that should NEVER be removed. Removing these breaks Windows or other critical apps. Keys are matched with PowerShell -like against the candidate's identifier (see Test-CanRemovePackage), so a key MAY contain wildcards - that is how whole framework families (Microsoft.VCLibs.*, Microsoft.NET.Native.*) are covered by one entry. This file is the ONLY hard block on removal, so anything a broad detection wildcard could sweep up must be listed here.

os_shell_and_logon._comment: Removing any of these can leave the machine unable to log in, render a Start menu, or prompt for credentials. Several are reachable from existing broad patterns - e.g. Microsoft.XboxGameCallableUI is matched by the 'Microsoft.Xbox*' bloatware pattern.

Microsoft.XboxGameCallableUI.reason: System UI component matched by the broad Microsoft.Xbox* pattern; not the Game Bar and not removable safely

Microsoft.AAD.BrokerPlugin.reason: Entra/Azure AD authentication broker; removing breaks work-account sign-in

Microsoft.AccountsControl.reason: Account/credential UI used by sign-in and UAC flows

Microsoft.CredDialogHost.reason: Credential dialog host; removing breaks authentication prompts

Microsoft.LockApp.reason: Lock screen; removing can make the machine unlockable

Microsoft.Windows.ShellExperienceHost.reason: Core shell (taskbar, action center, Start surfaces)

Microsoft.Windows.PeopleExperienceHost.reason: Shell contact surface; removal destabilises Explorer

Microsoft.Windows.ContentDeliveryManager.reason: Removing breaks Start/lock-screen content plumbing; suppress its CONTENT via the telemetry registry baseline instead

Microsoft.Win32WebViewHost.reason: Desktop app web view host used by system dialogs

Microsoft.Windows.CapturePicker.reason: System capture picker used by screen-sharing APIs

frameworks_and_runtimes._comment: Framework packages other apps declare as dependencies. Removing one silently breaks every app that depends on it. Wildcard keys cover all versions.

Microsoft.VCLibs.*.reason: Visual C++ UWP runtime; a declared dependency of very many Store apps (incl. winget)

Microsoft.UI.Xaml.*.reason: WinUI XAML framework; a declared dependency of many Store apps (incl. winget)

Microsoft.DesktopAppInstaller.reason: THIS IS WINGET. Removing it disables the package manager this project depends on for install/upgrade/uninstall

Microsoft.StorePurchaseApp.reason: Store purchase plumbing; removing breaks Store transactions

media_codecs._comment: Codec extensions. Photos/Camera/Media Player silently fail on common file types without them.

Microsoft.HEIFImageExtension.reason: HEIF/HEIC image support used by Photos

Microsoft.Advertising.Xaml.reason: Required by many UWP apps; removing breaks app compatibility

Microsoft.WindowsStore.reason: Microsoft Store; removing breaks app installation

Microsoft.Windows.SecHealthUI.reason: Security Dashboard UI; required for system security reporting

dmwappushservice.reason: Required by Windows Update and Intune telemetry

Microsoft.WindowsTerminal.reason: Modern terminal for PowerShell; development tool

Microsoft.Windows.Photos.reason: Default image viewer; removing leaves no in-box way to open pictures

Microsoft.Paint.reason: Classic Paint (NOT Paint 3D, which is Microsoft.MSPaint/Microsoft.Paint3D and IS removed)

Microsoft.MicrosoftStickyNotes.reason: Holds user-created notes; removal is data loss

MicrosoftCorporationII.QuickAssist.reason: Remote assistance tool used for support on unattended machines

Microsoft.SecHealthUI.reason: Windows Security UI (alternate package id to Microsoft.Windows.SecHealthUI)

Microsoft.MicrosoftEdge*.reason: Edge itself is the fallback browser and is servicing-managed; only Microsoft.Edge.GameAssist is treated as bloatware

Microsoft.OneDrive.reason: Removing can orphan synced user data; out of scope for unattended maintenance

Microsoft.Paint.reason: Can be removed if Paint 3D provides equivalent

Microsoft.People.reason: Contact management; can remove if not using Mail

Microsoft.WindowsAlarms.reason: Clock and alarm utility; can remove
